quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

options.text: Half as likely
Twice as likely
Three times as likely
Just as likely

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because:

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: The driver may not see you in their blind spot. They could change lanes suddenly without warning. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If someone follows you too closely, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Stay focused on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster, increasing danger. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers don't expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is especially important in areas where hazards are likely.

questions.question: Why should you use both front and rear brakes every time you slow or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake causes uneven wear.
It creates good braking habits for emergencies.
Both brakes are the only way to slow a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: It creates good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes in normal stops builds a habit you will need in emergencies. This habit can be critical when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can stop other vehicles from sharing their lane by:

options.text: Riding on the left side of the lane.
Riding in the center of the lane.
Giving dirty looks to drivers moving into the lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to prevent other drivers from trying to squeeze in beside you.

questions.question: The rear brake control is usually located:

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is controlled with your right foot.

questions.question: To see better before passing a vehicle on its left, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane to see ahead better and be more visible to oncoming traffic when preparing to pass.

questions.question: For routine braking:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Alternate between front and rear brakes to extend brake life.
Always use both front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: Experienced riders use "SIPDE" to stay aware of road conditions. What does the "E" stand for?

options.text: Explain
Error
Execute
Early

questions.correctAnswerText: Execute
questions.explanation: SIPDE is a five-step process: Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute. Experienced riders use it to make decisions and take action while riding.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle for a turn, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.
Apply the front brake.
Apply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make this happen.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?

options.text: By the left handgrip
By the right handgrip
By the left footrest
By the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip
questions.explanation: Know the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you start riding. The horn button is usually located by the left handgrip.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Tailgate other drivers.
Keep your eyes focused no more than 15 feet in front of your motorcycle.
Not use a headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible, signal your intentions, keep safe distance, look ahead, identify hazards, and be ready to react.

questions.question: When making a turn:

options.text: There is less traction available for stopping.
There is more traction available for stopping.
Stopping is no different than on a straight road.
You should never attempt to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less traction available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but you must be careful. When a motorcycle leans to turn, some traction is used for turning. This means less traction is available for stopping.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze only the front brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow or stop. This habit makes it easier to apply both brakes in an emergency stop.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Decrease your distance from the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Be flexible about your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies in poor conditions.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best way to stay close while keeping a safe distance is to ride:

options.text: In pairs.
In a staggered formation.
In a single-file line.
In a passing formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving all riders enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride single-file.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: Although staggered formation is usually best, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: A group of riders should pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a pyramid formation.
One at a time.
In a splintered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before passing. This pattern continues until all riders have passed safely.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far back on the seat so you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not support you. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to help with balance.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, what is usually safest?

options.text: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Riding straight within your lane to cross the tracks is dangerous.
It is not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Ride on the shoulder of the road to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When railroad tracks cross your lane at an angle, ride straight across them within your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could move into another lane of traffic.

questions.question: When are successful motorcyclists safest?

options.text: When they are seen by other motorists.
When they are faster than other vehicles.
When they are on the side of the road.
When they are in the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When they are seen by other motorists.
questions.explanation: Successful motorcyclists are safest when other drivers can clearly see them. Use your headlight, brake light, signals, and lane position to be more visible.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal on a motorcycle is usually located near the right footrest.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever on a motorcycle is usually located on the left handgrip.
